title: On the Complexity of Finding Fixed Points for Set-Valued Contractions
summary: In this paper, we study the computational complexity of finding fixed points for set-valued contractions. We first formulate a computational problem for Nadler's fixed-point theorem: Projected-Nadler, and prove that it is $\mathsf{CLS}$-complete by showing its equivalence to Continuous-LocalOpt. We then establish a stronger converse for Nadler's fixed point theorem that can be applied as a tool to analyze the convergence rate of set-valued basic iteration procedure. Finally, we reduce large-margin triplet stationarity problem to Projected-Nadler. Together with its $\mathsf{CLS}$-hardness…
